Where it began

Ben Stokes was born in Christchurch, New Zealand, on 4 June 1991. His father, Gerard Stokes, was a rugby league player and coach, and in 2003, when Ben was 12, he took the head coach's job at Workington Town, and the family made a new home in Cockermouth, in West Cumbria.

Ben went to Cockermouth School and learned his cricket at the local club, helping them to a league title in 2006 when he was only 15. Durham soon noticed. On his List A debut for them in 2009 he dismissed Mark Ramprakash with his third ball in professional cricket, which is one way to introduce yourself.

The player

Stokes was a left-handed middle-order batter and a right-arm fast bowler. His Test debut came in the 2013–14 Ashes, and at the WACA he made 120, England's only hundred of that series. Two years later at Cape Town he hit 258, the highest Test score by anyone batting at six, and shared a world-record stand of 399 with Jonny Bairstow.

He played 122 Tests between 2013 and 2026, making 7,273 runs at 34.47 with 14 hundreds, and taking 252 wickets at 30.98, with a best of six for 22. He also held 115 catches, and finished with 138 sixes, more than anyone else in Test history. His international career ended in June 2026, at Trent Bridge.

What made him special

Stokes was at his best when things looked worst. At Headingley in 2019, in a match where England had made just 67 first time round, he made 135 not out to see them home in a record chase of 359. Wisden named it the finest hundred of the decade. That same summer he top-scored for England in the World Cup final and was named player of the match.

In April 2022 he became Test captain, and with the coach Brendon McCullum he built the bold, attacking style people came to call Bazball. He led England in 44 Tests, winning 24. Only two of them were drawn, which tells you that a quiet afternoon of blocking was never really his idea of a good time.

Away from the middle

His public honours were many. He was BBC Sports Personality of the Year and the ICC's Cricketer of the Year in 2019, and was appointed OBE in the 2020 New Year Honours. Wisden named him its Leading Cricketer in the World three times, for 2019, 2020 and 2022, and in 2019 he was given the Freedom of the Borough of Allerdale. He also won a second World Cup in 2022, with 52 not out in the T20 final.

And finally

Back at Durham in May 2022 he made 161 from 88 balls against Worcestershire, including five sixes in a row in a single over. The last ball of that over bounced once before it reached the rope, so he had to settle for 34 from the over. Even the best-laid overs sometimes fall one bounce short.
